question: The committed circuits are fixed at four bids. How do the REP3 (coNoir) circuits and the settlement grow with N bids?
method: scripts/measure_bid_scaling.py derives N-bid variants of the three committed coNoir circuits under ignored .local/ (only the bid count changes; the settlement plan has N + 2 rows), compiles them with the pinned Noir 1.0.0-rc.2, and counts UltraHonk gates with the pinned bb. The four-bid variants match the committed circuits gate for gate and opcode for opcode. With --mpc it runs the clearing circuit three-party REP3 on synthetic bids (95, 90, ... above reserve 20, units N - 1), then verifies the proof.
machine: shared 16 GiB Apple M1, three parties on one host, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2, heavy swap from other applications

clearing_rep3_16_bids.basis: not run: about 2.5 GiB per party times three would not fit beside the other workloads on this shared machine. Proof time scales with the padded circuit size (16,384 -> 32,768 rows took x2.12; 131,072 rows is two more doublings); witness time scales with ACIR opcodes; memory scales linearly with padded size between the two measured points.

settlement_bindings.rows: N + 2 (N refunds, the seller, the operator fee)
settlement_bindings.basis: browser run of Oct 18 (evidence/2026-10-18-fresh-book-native-settlement.json): binding key 130.5 -> 241.7 s, six rows 241.7 -> 786.3 s
settlement_bindings.rows_are_independent: yes in the protocol (one row, one note); the prototype proves them one after another

reading: The quadratic part, all-pairs ranking inside the joint proof, stays in seconds: 3.1 s at four bids, 6.5 s at eight, about 30 s estimated at sixteen. The dominant settlement cost is one Halo2 binding per output, linear in N and independent per row, so it can run in parallel across cores or operators; the prototype runs the rows one after another. Four bids is the committed circuit size, not a performance limit. Beyond a few dozen bids, all-pairs ranking (about 320 gates per bid pair, fitted to the three sizes) should give way to a sorting network.
